source_caption:
Shooter — A Sniper Betrayed

Shooter (2007) follows Bob Lee Swagger, a highly skilled former Marine sniper who has withdrawn from society after a mission ends in tragedy. Living in isolation, Swagger wants nothing more than to stay away from the world he once served.

His quiet life changes when a government official approaches him with a dangerous assignment. Swagger is asked to use his expertise to prevent an assassination attempt against the President. Believing that he is helping his country, he agrees to take the job.

But the mission turns into a setup. Swagger is framed for a crime he didn't commit and suddenly finds himself hunted by the same people who recruited him. Forced to disappear, he uses his military skills to uncover who betrayed him and why.

As Swagger searches for the truth, he realizes that the conspiracy reaches far beyond a single assassination. With powerful people determined to silence him, he must stay ahead of those pursuing him while gathering enough evidence to expose the operation.

The film explores themes of betrayal, loyalty, corruption, survival, and justice. Swagger's fight becomes more than a mission—it's a battle to clear his name and expose the people who used him.

What makes Shooter compelling is its combination of tactical action, conspiracy, and a protagonist who refuses to be eliminated quietly.

💬 They thought they had the perfect sniper. They didn't expect him to survive the setup.

source_details.synopsis: Shooter is a 2007 American action thriller film directed by Antoine Fuqua and written by Jonathan Lemkin, based on the 1993 novel Point of Impact by Stephen Hunter. The film follows Force Recon Marine Scout Sniper veteran Bob Lee Swagger (Mark Wahlberg), who is framed for murder by a mercenary unit operating for a private military firm. The film also stars Michael Peña, Danny Glover, Kate Mara, Levon Helm, and Ned Beatty. Shooter was produced by Lorenzo di Bonaventura through di Bonaventura Pictures, and released by Paramount Pictures in the United States on March 23, 2007. The film received mixed reviews and grossed $95.7 million on a $61 million budget.
